name: Fuel pump
summary: An electric pump, usually inside the fuel tank, that sends fuel forward to the engine.
whatItDoes: It supplies fuel to the engine at the pressure the injectors need.
howItWorks: An electric motor sitting in the fuel drives a small pump, and the fuel around it keeps it cool. Many direct-injection petrol engines also have a second, mechanical high-pressure pump on the engine. The in-tank pump is often reached through an access panel under the rear seat, or from below with the tank lowered.
failureSymptoms: The engine cranks but won't start
Hesitation or loss of power under load
Whining from the rear of the car
safetyNotes: Petrol vapour is extremely flammable. Work outdoors or somewhere well ventilated, with no flames or sparks.
Relieve the fuel pressure and disconnect the battery before opening any fuel line.
Diesel high-pressure systems run at very high pressure. Leave them to a professional.
